title: Run a reduction in force
summary: A reduction in force is a legal process wrapped around a painful decision, so do the paperwork in the right order. Write the business case and the selection criteria before any names, and review the resulting list for adverse impact. Check the statutory notice floors early: under the federal WARN Act, an employer with 100 or more employees may not order a plant closing or mass layoff until 60 days after written notice (law rule us-fed.warn-notice), and several states run mini-WARN acts with lower thresholds. Plan final pay by state; in California final wages are due at the termination itself, with waiting-time penalties for lateness (law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing). For anyone 40 or older, a release of federal age claims only works inside the OWBPA windows: at least 21 days to consider (45 for a group program), a 7-day revocation period, and the group disclosures (law rule us-fed.owbpa-release-windows). Then run one humane day: managers briefed first, affected people told first and in person, the company the same day, each offboarding executed cleanly, and the survivors given the real math once. Educational guidance, not legal advice; employment counsel reviews the plan before anyone hears a word.

parts.title: Write the business case and the selection criteria before any names: roles not people, then an adverse-impact review of the resulting list

execution.rationale: Leadership defines the criteria and selects against them, and employment counsel reviews the list for adverse impact; the selection judgment is the legally exposed act.

parts.title: Check the statutory notice floors against your real counts: employees, sites, and the 60-day federal clock
parts.guidance: The federal WARN Act binds employers with 100 or more employees ordering a plant closing or mass layoff: 60 days' written notice to affected employees or their representatives, the state dislocated-worker unit, and the chief elected local official, with the statute's reduced-notice exceptions (law rule us-fed.warn-notice). Whether this layoff crosses the headcount and single-site percentage tests is a counsel determination, and state mini-WARN acts set lower floors.

geoResolutions.label: The WARN Act's 100-employee floor and 60-day notice (law rule us-fed.warn-notice), plus the state mini-WARN acts the rule's caveat flags

Dismissals run under the Fair Work Act: unfair-dismissal exposure begins after the minimum employment period (law rule au.unfair-dismissal-minimum-period), and genuine-redundancy requirements shape the selection and consultation
Statutory severance is part of the cost of every separation: an employee with a year or more of service is owed roughly 30 days' average wages per year of service (law rule kr.severance-pay)

execution.rationale: Compute the headcounts, site totals, and percentage tests from the supplied HR records against the cited statutory thresholds; counsel reads the result.

parts.title: Plan final pay by state for every affected person: some clocks run at the termination itself
parts.guidance: California requires final wages, including accrued vacation, at the termination when the employer discharges, with a waiting-time penalty of a day's wages per day late up to 30 days (law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing). Map each affected person's state and schedule the final-pay runs so no clock is missed on the day.

execution.rationale: Map each affected person's work state and accrued balances from the payroll records into a final-pay schedule for the payroll owner to execute.

parts.title: Draft severance and releases with the statutory windows built in: 21 or 45 days to consider, 7 to revoke, group disclosures for 40-plus
parts.guidance: A release of federal age-discrimination claims by anyone 40 or older is only knowing and voluntary inside the OWBPA conditions: at least 21 days to consider, 45 days when the waiver rides a group termination program, a 7-day revocation period before effectiveness, and the written group disclosures of the decisional unit, eligibility factors, and the ages and titles selected and not selected (law rule us-fed.owbpa-release-windows). Severance in exchange for the release is the standard trade; counsel drafts it.

execution.rationale: Employment counsel drafts the separation agreements and disclosures; the statutory windows make the drafting a legal act rather than a template fill.

parts.title: Plan the day: managers briefed first, affected people told first and in person, the company the same day, benefits and payroll logistics ready

execution.rationale: The founder and managers deliver the news personally and in sequence; the logistics plan exists so the conversations are the only hard part left on the day.

parts.title: Run each offboarding cleanly: access, devices, final pay on the state's clock, benefits paperwork

execution.rationale: The offboarding scope includes physical device return alongside digital access revocation and the per-state final-pay administration; the referenced record carries the mechanics.

parts.title: Give the survivors the real math once: what was cut, why, and the plan the smaller team is now running

execution.rationale: The founder explains the reduction to the remaining team directly and answers questions; credibility with the survivors is personal work.

metadata.trigger: The decision is made: the plan no longer supports the team, and a reduction in force is how the company survives.
metadata.supportReason: Selection, the releases, and the conversations are counsel and founder work; an agent can compute the WARN thresholds from the HR records and build the per-state final-pay schedule.

contextNeeded.query: headcount by site and work state, including part-time status
